body:
You are drafting DIALOGUE TEXT for a video game. Reply in plain text only, in exactly the format asked at the end.

"The Crooked Moon" is a single-player, turn-based tactical party RPG (think Baldur's Gate 3: fully voiced, branching dialogue, skill checks, a storyteller Narrator). It is folk horror set in Druskenvald, an afterlife realm of endless night under a gargantuan crescent moon with a leering crone's face; an autumn that never ends, pumpkins and bonfires and dead leaves everywhere, but the stakes are real. Humour is deadpan and sits beside the dread. Use only the names given here; invent no new named people, places, monsters or history.

THE PARTY: the player leads four heroes; never name, describe or gender the player's heroes. Some of the party may be these companions, who speak only in the `interject` lines written for them (each line is said only if that companion is present, so it must make sense on its own and never answer another companion's line):
- rook_coldwake: Rook, a Graveborn (undead) fighter, a graveyard rest warden; dry, level, practical, union-minded, cares that the dead are laid to rest properly; few words.
- tobin_hayward: Tobin, a Harvestborn (living scarecrow of wicker and straw) druid; brisk, warm, country-wise, talks about rot, roots, harvests and neighbours; kind under the sharp tongue.
- silas_vane: Silas, a Relicborn (skeleton-folk) monk and card sharp from river landings; fast, cocky, thinks in odds, bets and marks.
- delphine_ravelle: Delphine, a Threadborn (living patchwork doll) warlock; theatrical vaudeville showwoman, says "darling", treats horror as a third-rate sideshow she means to headline.
- lucan_houndstooth: Lucan, a Curseborn (wolf-man) ranger and monster hunter; hushed and earnest, narrates danger like a nature broadcaster, notices scents and tracks.
- cordelia_skein: Cordelia, a Silkborn (spider-folk) sorcerer; cool, cultivated, clinical, delighted by anything morbid as a subject of study.

RULES FOR THE TEXT
- Spoken lines: 1 to 3 short sentences, about 12 to 30 words, never over 40. Contractions are normal. People talk in their own voice and do not explain the plot to the audience. Accent is word choice and rhythm, never phonetic spelling. Country folk of the Hollow speak with a folksy country drawl in their word choice.
- Interject lines: one sentence, under 20 words.
- Option lines (what the player's party says or does): under 12 words, plain, in the party's voice ("We..." or an imperative).
- Narrator lines (the Vagrant, an old train conductor telling the tale afterwards: warm, folksy, wry, a Southern drawl in word choice such as reckon, ain't, folks, a spell, a piece; drop a final g in at most one line in three): second person, present tense, one or two sentences, only what a hero could perceive, concrete senses (smell, sound, texture, cold), no game words (HP, roll, level, check, DC, save, hit points), never tell the player what to feel, never the word "suddenly", never mention a fiddle, never name the Vagrant.
- No stage directions, asterisks, italics, brackets, placeholders, emoji or em dashes (use commas, periods, colons). Straight quotes only. Do not use the arrow characters -> or => inside the text.
- Content is dark but restrained: no gore, no graphic detail.
- Each brief says what the line must do; keep its facts, write it as the speaker would say it.

THIS SCENE: short meetings on the roads of Wickermoor Hollow later in the story, played while the party travels between places on the map. Wickermoor Village is the hub. East is Foxwillow, a farming town; north-west, up the Silverbell river road in the foothills of the Howlers mountains, is the mining village of Dawn's Gate under the Crimson Monastery, whose monks wear red; south, through a swamp, is the Drowned Crossroads with its gambling riverboat, ruled by a grinning deal-maker called Mister Crossroads; north-west up a hill trail is Glitterdeep Mine, where a plague of centipedes is spreading; far west across a marsh, on Moonsong Lake, is Memory's Rest, a sanatorium run by Matron Lethica; south-east is Maidenmist, a fogbound cemetery.

Speakers (besides the Narrator and the companions above):
- road_refugee: a Foxwillow farm wife fleeing her burning town with her family and a handcart; hoarse, frightened, decent.
- road_pilgrim: a barefoot woman pilgrim climbing to the Crimson Monastery to be cleansed of sin; earnest, glowing, naive.
- road_dice_ghost: a drowned gambler's ghost on a swamp causeway, waistcoat soaked, rattling dice; friendly as a card sharp, sad underneath.
- road_miner: a Glitterdeep miner sick with the plague, centipedes under his skin; scared, ashamed, kind.
- road_patient: an escaped sanatorium patient in a hospital gown, serene and smiling, who has lost his name and memories to the Matron's medicine.
- road_mourner: a woman leading a funeral to Maidenmist with an empty coffin; quiet, worn out, steady.

The meetings (the [[n]] markers in this file are yours; everything else is fixed):

```
# Meetings on the roads of Acts II and III (data/random_encounters/foxwillow_road, silverbell_road, bayou_road, skitter_road,
# marsh_road and cemetery_road): each plays once on its table's map, then the journey goes on. Fun pass lane D.
# Drafted by Gemini (docs/plans/gemini_roads), edited; flags in data/flags/roads.json.

# --- Refugees from Foxwillow ---

~ foxwillow_refugees
set road_refugees_met
appear road_refugee
Narrator: [[1]]
road_refugee [afraid]: [[2]]
interject name:tobin_hayward: [[3]]
-> fr_menu

~ fr_menu
* [if gold >= 5] [[4]] -> fr_give
* [Medicine DC 12] [[5]] -> fr_tend | fr_tend_fail
* [if not flag.road_refugees_asked] [[6]] -> fr_ask
* [[7]] -> fr_leave

~ fr_give
gold -5
road_refugee [sad]: [[8]]
approve tobin_hayward +2 rook_coldwake +1: You gave a burnt-out family from Foxwillow coin for the road
-> END

~ fr_tend
road_refugee [sad]: [[9]]
Narrator: [[10]]
approve tobin_hayward +1 cordelia_skein +1: You dressed a refugee child's burns on the road
-> END

~ fr_tend_fail
Narrator: [[11]]
-> fr_menu

~ fr_ask
set road_refugees_asked
road_refugee: [[12]]
road_refugee [afraid]: [[13]]
-> fr_menu

~ fr_leave
road_refugee: [[14]]
-> END

# --- A pilgrim bound for the Crimson Monastery ---

~ crimson_pilgrim
set road_pilgrim_met
appear road_pilgrim
Narrator: [[15]]
road_pilgrim [smile]: [[16]]
interject name:delphine_ravelle: [[17]]
-> cp_menu

~ cp_menu
* [Persuasion DC 14] [[18]] -> cp_turn | cp_on
* [if not flag.road_pilgrim_asked] [[19]] -> cp_ask
* [[20]] -> cp_let

~ cp_turn
set road_pilgrim_turned
road_pilgrim [afraid]: [[21]]
Narrator: [[22]]
approve rook_coldwake +1 tobin_hayward +1: You talked a pilgrim out of climbing to the Crimson Monastery
-> END

~ cp_on
road_pilgrim [angry]: [[23]]
Narrator: [[24]]
-> END

~ cp_ask
set road_pilgrim_asked
road_pilgrim: [[25]]
road_pilgrim [smile]: [[26]]
-> cp_menu

~ cp_let
road_pilgrim [smile]: [[27]]
-> END

# --- A dead gambler wants a game ---

~ dice_ghost
set road_dice_met
appear road_dice_ghost
Narrator: [[28]]
road_dice_ghost [sly]: [[29]]
interject name:silas_vane: [[30]]
-> dg_menu

~ dg_menu
* [if gold >= 5] [Insight DC 13] [[31]] -> dg_win | dg_lose
* [if not flag.road_dice_asked] [[32]] -> dg_ask
* [[33]] -> dg_leave

~ dg_win
gold +10
road_dice_ghost [angry]: [[34]]
Narrator: [[35]]
approve silas_vane +2: You called a dead man's bluff at Liar's Dice
-> END

~ dg_lose
gold -5
road_dice_ghost [smile]: [[36]]
Narrator: [[37]]
-> END

~ dg_ask
set road_dice_asked
road_dice_ghost: [[38]]
road_dice_ghost [sad]: [[39]]
-> dg_menu

~ dg_leave
road_dice_ghost [sly]: [[40]]
-> END

```

Briefs for the markers:
1. narrator: a family comes down the Foxwillow road with a handcart piled with bedding, a woman, an old man and two children, smelling of smoke, the sky behind them orange
2. road_refugee: a Foxwillow farm wife, hoarse; Foxwillow is burning, neighbour set against neighbour, they got out with what they could carry; she asks if Wickermoor is far
3. interject tobin_hayward: smoke in the bedding and ash in the children's hair; that's a whole harvest gone up
4. option: give them five gold for the road
5. option: look at the children's burns
6. option: ask what happened in Foxwillow
7. option: wish them luck and go on
8. road_refugee: she closes her hand on the coins and cannot speak for a moment; she says she will remember the faces of folk who stopped
9. road_refugee: she thanks them, it's more than the doctor in Foxwillow would do now, he's barred his door like the rest
10. narrator: you clean the burns with water from your flasks and bind them with a strip of clean linen; the smaller child stops crying and falls asleep on the bedding
11. narrator: the boy flinches away from your hands, and his grandfather pulls him back onto the cart without a word
12. road_refugee: the families have been at each other for years, but this is different; folk are telling secrets on each other they never knew they knew
13. road_refugee: she whispers that it's the crows; there are crows on every roof and every fence, and whatever you say near them, somebody else knows by morning
14. road_refugee: Wickermoor's that way, then; she thanks them and puts her shoulder to the cart
15. narrator: on the road up into the foothills a woman in a plain grey shift walks barefoot, a red cord tied round her wrist and her shoes in her hand
16. road_pilgrim: a pilgrim, glowing with purpose; she is climbing to the Crimson Monastery to be cleansed of her sins, the brothers say there's nothing left of a sinner afterwards but peace
17. interject delphine_ravelle: nothing left of her but peace; darling, I have read that review before, and the show was ghastly
18. option: tell her not to go up there
19. option: ask about the monastery
20. option: let her go on her way
21. road_pilgrim: she stops, uncertain; she had thought it strange the ones who went up never wrote home; she will go back down and think on it
22. narrator: she unties the red cord from her wrist and lets the wind take it down the slope, and turns back the way she came, slow, then quicker
23. road_pilgrim: she says sin always talks like that, sweet and reasonable, the brothers warned her; she pulls away and climbs faster
24. narrator: she goes on up the road without looking back; above, a bell in the monastery tolls once, as if it heard her coming
25. road_pilgrim: the brothers wear red and sing all night; the abbot was a knight once, a golden knight, and now he has given himself to his goddess entirely
26. road_pilgrim: they say his goddess is very beautiful, and very hungry for the good in people; she is not sure what that means but she says it sounds holy
27. road_pilgrim: bless you, and she hopes they find someone to cleanse them too, one day
28. narrator: on a stump at the edge of the causeway sits a man in a gambler's waistcoat, soaked through and green at the edges, rattling dice in a cup; water runs out of his sleeves
29. road_dice_ghost: a drowned gambler, friendly as a card sharp; a little game of Liar's Dice to pass the night, five gold a throw, he has nothing but time
30. interject silas_vane: a dead man with a dice cup; watch his left hand, that's where the sixes live
31. option: play him for five gold
32. option: ask how he came to be here
33. option: decline the game
34. road_dice_ghost: he slaps the stump; nobody has called him on a bluff in forty years; he pays up with coins green with weed
35. narrator: he empties his cup out onto the stump and three of the dice roll into the water without a splash
36. road_dice_ghost: he laughs, a wet laugh; the house always wins, friend, even out here; he rakes in the coins
37. narrator: the coins sink into his palm like stones into a pond, and his grin gets wider by exactly one tooth
38. road_dice_ghost: he lost a game at the Drowned Crossroads to a gentleman with a big grin; the stakes were not money; he's been working off his marker ever since
39. road_dice_ghost: Mister Crossroads holds his soul in a pocket, he says; the debt never gets smaller, it only changes shape
40. road_dice_ghost: suit yourselves; he'll be here when they come back, he's always here

## Reply format
One line per marker, in order, exactly `n => text` (no quotes around the text, no extra lines, no commentary). 40 lines, numbered as above.
result:
1 => Down the Foxwillow road comes a woman pullin' a handcart piled high with bedding, an old man and two children trailing behind. They smell sharp of woodsmoke, and the sky at their backs is glowing mean and orange.
2 => Please, is it much further to Wickermoor? Whole of Foxwillow is burning down, neighbour turned on neighbour, and we only got out with what the cart could hold.
3 => Smoke in the quilts and ash in the young ones' hair, that is a whole season's keeping gone to cinder.
4 => Take these five gold pieces for the road.
5 => Let us look at the children's burns.
6 => What happened back in Foxwillow?
7 => We wish you luck on the road.
8 => I don't know what to say to that, truly I don't. I will remember the faces of the folk who stopped for us tonight.
9 => Thank you kindly, that is more than our own doctor in Foxwillow would do. He barred his door tight like all the rest when the shouting started.
10 => You wash the soot from the blisters with cold flask water and bind them up in clean linen. The smaller child quits whimpering, leans into the piled quilts, and goes fast asleep.
11 => The boy jerks back from the reach of your hands, and his granddaddy hauls him up onto the cart bed without a word.
12 => Our families have feuded for years, sure, but never like this. Folks are shouting out dark secrets on their neighbours that they had no earthly way of knowing.
13 => Keep your voice down, because it's the crows doing it. They sit thick on every roof and fence rail, and whatever you whisper near them, the whole town knows by morning.
14 => Just down the road a piece, then. We thank you kindly, friends, and we best keep moving.
15 => Up where the road climbs into the rocky foothills, a barefoot woman comes walking in a plain grey shift. She carries her worn shoes in one hand, a bright red cord tied neat around her wrist.
16 => Good evening to you, travellers, and may the high road bless your steps. I'm climbing to the Crimson Monastery to have my sins washed away, for the brothers promise nothing is left of a sinner afterward but peace.
17 => Nothing left of her but peace, darling, I have read that exact notice before and the show was positively ghastly.
18 => Do not go up to that monastery.
19 => Tell us about the Crimson Monastery.
20 => Go on your way in peace.
21 => You sound awful sure of that, and I admit I always wondered why the folk who climbed up never wrote home again. Maybe I'll walk back down a spell and think on it.
22 => Her fingers work the knot of the red cord loose from her wrist and let the cold wind carry it down the slope. She turns back the way she came, slow at first, then quickenin' her step.
23 => The brothers warned me that sin always talks just like you, sweet and reasonable on the tongue. I won't let you turn me from my cleansing now.
24 => She pulls away and climbs higher up the stones without looking back. High above in the dark, a heavy monastery bell tolls once through the cold air.
25 => The brothers up there wear red robes and sing hymns through the whole blessed night. Folks say the abbot was a golden knight once, before he gave himself over entirely to his goddess.
26 => They say his goddess is terrible and lovely to behold, and awful hungry for the good in people. I don't rightly know what that means, yet it sure sounds holy to me.
27 => Bless your hearts for stopping to talk. I hope you find someone to wash your own souls clean one day soon.
28 => Out on a rotten stump by the causeway's edge sits a man in a soaked waistcoat gone green with pond scum. Cold swamp water drips steady from his cuffs while he rattles bone dice inside a leather cup.
29 => Evening, friends, care to rattle the bones for five gold a throw to help pass the night? Sit yourselves down for a friendly hand of Liar's Dice, I've got nothing left in the world but time.
30 => A drowned sharp rattling a cup, watch his left hand close because that's where the sixes live.
31 => We'll play you for five gold.
32 => How did you end up on this causeway?
33 => We'll pass on the game tonight.
34 => Well now, ain't a living soul called me on that bluff in forty wet years. Take your winnings, fair and square, even if the pond weed has turned the gold a touch green.
35 => He tips his leather cup upside down over the wet stump. Three of the bone dice tumble off the bark and drop into the black water without a single splash.
36 => That's the way the river runs, friends, the house always takes its cut even out here in the reeds. Come back whenever your pockets feel too heavy.
37 => Your warm coins sink straight into his wet palm like pebbles dropped in a pond. His pale grin stretches wider by the breadth of a single yellow tooth.
38 => I sat down at the Drowned Crossroads once across from a gentleman with a mighty wide grin. We weren't playing for coin that night, and I've been sitting on this stump working off my marker ever since.
39 => Mister Crossroads keeps my soul tucked down in his waistcoat pocket like a brass watch. No matter how many hands I win out here, that debt never gets an inch smaller, it only changes its shape.
40 => Suit yourselves, travellers, and mind your boots on the slick boards. I'll still be sitting right here when you come back through, I'm always here.
